title: Case: Delivery photo shows a house the recipient does not recognise
context: Oswin Brackley of 23 Pellow Street ordered a cordless strimmer from Thistlecombe Goods (TG-1668 / DL-6827). The desk raised his report with the carrier two days ago.
initial_request: I GOT AN EMAIL TELLING ME TO CONTACT BRINELEAF PANTRY. I have never bought ANYTHING from Brineleaf Pantry. I rang them anyway, 25 minutes on hold, they have no order, no record, never heard of me. Obviously. I bought it from TALLOWMERE. Your 'claim' is CLOSED. Meanwhile my parcel is sat in some stranger's porch, two days now. I do not want another form or another company's phone number. I want a HUMAN BEING at that depot to LOOK AT THE PHOTO and go and GET IT.

events.body: DL-6827 delivered 11:02. Photo captured at stop. Left in porch.
THAT IS NOT MY HOUSE. the photo shows a green door and a gravel drive with a porch. I live in a terrace. No drive. No porch. Blue door. Nothing on Pellow Street looks like that. where is my strimmer

events.to: Parcel trace team, Ashgrove Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-6827: delivered scan 11:02 today with a photo. The recipient, Oswin Brackley, 23 Pellow Street, says the photo shows a different property (green door, gravel drive, porch; his is a terraced house with none of these). Please trace.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Ashgrove Arc Logistics
events.body: Ticket PT-7730 closed. Reason: shipper-managed claims account. No trace opened. The recipient has been emailed and advised to contact the shipper, Brineleaf Pantry.

Answering your query: TG-1668 is our order, picked and shipped from our warehouse on 9 June under our Ashgrove Arc account as DL-6827. Brineleaf Pantry has nothing to do with it and would have no record of it.

Saw PT-7730. For next time: Parcel trace only does in-network losses and their queue auto-closes on the shipper field, which looks wrong on this one. A delivered scan with a photo of the wrong property is Delivery investigations, by Email. They pull the stop GPS and can task the depot to send the driver back.

Suspected misdelivery, needs a stop review today: DL-6827 / TG-1668, Oswin Brackley, 23 Pellow Street (cordless strimmer, shipper Thistlecombe Goods). Delivered scan 11:02 on 12 June, 'left in porch', with a photo. The recipient says the photo is not his house: it shows a green door, a gravel drive and a porch; his is a terraced house with a blue door, no drive and no porch, and he says nothing on his street looks like it. I raised this with Parcel trace on 12 June; their ticket PT-7730 closed on 13 June with no trace opened, reason 'shipper-managed claims account', and he was emailed to contact Brineleaf Pantry. That is the wrong shipper. Thistlecombe Goods Warehouse dispatch confirm TG-1668 is theirs, shipped on their account. He rang Brineleaf, who have no record of him. So nothing has been looked at in two days and the parcel is presumably still at whatever address is in the photo. Please pull the stop GPS against the photo, and if it is a wrong address, task the depot with recovery. Please tell me what you find; I have not told him anything is under way.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Delivery investigations, Ashgrove Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tells Oswin Brackley to take it up with the seller (Thistlecombe Goods or Brineleaf Pantry) or to file another claim, as the next step
Describes the trace or claim as open, in progress or being investigated
Sends the report back to the Parcel trace team on the Depot work queue
Promises a refund, a replacement, or that the driver will retrieve the parcel
States as fact that the parcel is lost or stolen, or that it was delivered to his address
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3203: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 8) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's.
